note: Holmes and Watson walk slowly across the moor as the sun sinks behind the Mapleton stables. Holmes reasons out where the horse has gone (¶113–116).

label: Thursday evening, at the long hollow towards Mapleton
quote: a few more minutes brought us to the hollow in question
note: Holmes finds the horse's track and fits the horseshoe to it.

label: Thursday evening, picking up the tracks again close to Mapleton
quote: only to pick them up once more quite close to Mapleton
note: They cross the marshy bottom and the dry turf, and lose the tracks for half a mile. Here a man's track appears beside the horse's.

label: Thursday evening, following the double track towards King's Pyland
quote: we both followed along after it
note: Watson sees the same tracks coming back in the opposite direction.

label: Thursday evening, following the return track
quote: Let us follow the return track

label: Thursday evening, at the gates of the Mapleton stables
quote: It ended at the paving of asphalt which led up to the gates of the Mapleton stables
note: The groom runs out. Silas Brown comes out and Holmes whispers to him (¶124–135).

label: Thursday evening, Holmes and Silas Brown in the parlour
quote: Now, Mr. Brown, I am quite at your disposal
note: About twenty minutes (¶137). Watson waits outside.

label: Thursday evening, at dusk, Holmes and Silas Brown reappear
quote: It was twenty minutes, and the reds had all faded into greys before Holmes and the trainer reappeared
note: Brown promises Holmes his instructions will be done (¶138–143).

label: Thursday evening, setting off for King's Pyland
quote: we set off for King’s Pyland

label: Five o'clock the next morning, when Holmes speaks of calling on Silas Brown
quote: if I were to call at five o’clock to-morrow morning
note: Holmes puts this to the groom as a question. The text does not order it against the inquest or Holmes's study of his ground.

label: The next day, when Silas Brown shall hear from Holmes
quote: you shall hear from me to-morrow
note: Holmes also says 'I shall write to you about it' (¶141).

label: When what Silas Brown promises shall be there
note: This is promised and not dated. The text does not say what it is or where.

label: When the horse's track was made in the long hollow
quote: The track of a horse was plainly outlined in the soft earth
note: The text does not date it. Holmes supposes the horse crossed there after the tragedy, when the hollow 'must have been very wet on Monday night' (¶116). The horseshoe fits the print.

label: When a man's track came beside the horse's near Mapleton
quote: A man’s track was visible beside the horse’s
note: The horse was alone before this point along the trail (¶120–121).

label: When the double track turned off towards King's Pyland
quote: The double track turned sharp off and took the direction of King’s Pyland

label: When the same tracks came back to the Mapleton gates
quote: the same tracks coming back again in the opposite direction
note: The return track ends at the asphalt paving to the Mapleton gates (¶124).
